title: Strings as Reference Types
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and behavior of strings as reference types in C#.
Choose an appropriate type for a simple application scenario.

understand.concept: string is a reference type representing immutable text. A string variable can refer to a string object or, when nullable reference types are enabled, be declared as possibly null. String operations produce new strings rather than modifying the original text.
understand.whyItMatters: String values are used for names, messages, input and file data. Knowing that strings are immutable and reference types helps avoid null errors and unnecessary assumptions about mutation.
understand.analogy: A string is like a printed label: to change its wording, you produce a new label rather than editing the existing printed one.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not mean strings are stored in a special physical location; it describes the observable immutability of string values.

explain.narrative:
## string is a reference type

C# string is an alias for System.String. A string variable refers to a string object. String literals use double quotes, and a string can be null when its nullable reference annotation permits it.

## Immutability

String objects are immutable. Operations such as Replace, Trim and concatenation return string results; they do not mutate the original string object. Assign the returned result if you want to keep it.

## Comparing text

Use string.Equals or the appropriate comparison overload when comparison rules matter. Ordinal comparisons are useful for identifiers and machine-readable tokens; culture-aware comparisons are often better for user-facing language.

## Null handling

Use string.IsNullOrEmpty or string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace for common checks. The null-coalescing operator can provide a fallback. Nullable reference annotations help the compiler identify possible null dereferences.

## Baseline

Examples target .NET 10 and C# 14.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes string in C#?
questions.answer: It is an immutable reference type
options: It is an immutable reference type
It is a mutable value type
It is an array of char that can be changed in place
questions.explanation: string is a reference type and its contents cannot be changed after creation.

options: The same string modified in place
questions.explanation: String methods return results; they do not mutate the original string.

questions.prompt: What does nickname ?? "Guest" do when nickname is null?
questions.explanation: The null-coalescing operator evaluates the right operand when the left operand is null.

questions.prompt: Which method checks for null, empty or whitespace-only text?
questions.explanation: IsNullOrWhiteSpace covers null, empty and whitespace-only strings.
Length reports the number of UTF-16 code units, not necessarily user-perceived characters.
